depiction.composition: circular arrow curved around upper left with wrench badge at bottom right

readings.meaning: factory reset, restore default settings, or system recovery
revert configuration or roll back changes
repair, refurbish, or restore an item

ambiguity: Can be confused with a generic refresh, undo, or history icon at small sizes if the wrench is not clearly seen as a tool.
task_intents: factory reset a device or router
roll back a broken configuration change
run system recovery on a computer

example_tasks.task: Restore the garage door keypad to factory defaults before the new tenants move in
Reset BIOS settings on the gaming PC to stop the random memory crashes
Revert the nginx config changes from yesterday's deploy
Reset the service interval light on the Subaru after changing the oil
Re-initialize the smart thermostat and clear the old heating schedule
Run the monthly descaling and flush cycle on the espresso machine
Restore default brush presets in Procreate
Return all network flags to baseline
Put the original stock firmware back on before shipping
Hard reset the pair of Bluetooth earbuds that refuse to pair with my phone
Use the pinhole button on the NAS to reset the admin network settings without wiping drives

near_misses.better: key or lock with reset arrow

near_misses.task: Buy a factory-refurbished monitor for the home office

reasoning: A counterclockwise undo/reset arrow paired with a wrench specifically denotes resetting settings (factory reset, configuration rollback) or recurring maintenance. It fits technical and home maintenance tasks well, though it is narrower than a plain wrench for repairs or a plain arrow for returns.
